what_happened: Reproduced --prune --dry-run (not just --regenerate) against BimodalLogic's live stage-based specs/ROADMAP.md (~/Projects/BimodalLogic, current HEAD, deployed roadmap-integration.sh). Unlike --regenerate, --prune does NOT crash -- it exits 0 and the dry-run diff shows it would silently replace the entire ~280-line hand-curated Stage 0-4 / Not-scoped / Maintenance / Related content with the fixed 8-section empty skeleton (## Goal, ## Gate state, etc, all empty), because none of its extract_section() header literals match the file's actual headers. This sharpens sub-fault 3 (the overwrite near-miss) from a documented risk the dispatch's own EVIDENCE section did not test into a mechanically-confirmed, exit-0, silent, catastrophic-content-loss failure mode on the regression fixture itself -- more dangerous than the --regenerate crash because nothing signals a problem at all.

BimodalLogic's live specs/ROADMAP.md explicitly declares itself NOT the generator's format: its own ## Maintenance section states 'Hand-curated prose, not mechanically parsed or annotated', and its ## Related section lists core/context/formats/roadmap-format.md as 'the legacy parseable structure, superseded above'. Separately, its stage headers already drifted across two hand-edit commits during this research window alone (## Run order at a glance -> ## Next batches; Stage 1's parenthetical dropped) -- evidence the stage layout is not a stable closed vocabulary the way the original 8-section format is. This bears directly on what 'teach the generator the stage-based layout' should mean at plan time: a full structural round-trip of the Stage N bullet-prose is chasing an intentionally-unstable target, whereas the Run-order/Next-batches fenced /orchestrate block is structurally stable and generator-compatible. Flagged for the planner's judgment, not re-litigating the settled generated-artifact ruling.

Plan-time check of the stderr marker's consumers (test suite asserts it -->$-anchored; roadmap-update.md documents caller reliance on its counts and is out of this task's file scope) showed the research's suggested 'add a status=ok|error field' would have been a silent contract break reaching a file this task may not edit. Froze the six-field marker shape and delivered diagnosability via a separate ERR-trap ERROR: line instead -- same complaint satisfied, no out-of-scope drift.

plan-file-scope-harvest.sh run against the finished plan resolved exactly the intended four-file scope on the first try, and suite-selection-lib.sh resolved both the script and the format spec to test-roadmap-generation.sh (no __FULL_SWEEP__), so every non-final phase's Tier Justification names a real covering suite rather than a gate subset.
